hints.title: Target Element Rank
hints.text: For a matrix with m rows and n columns, the median is the value that has at least (m * n + 1) // 2 elements less than or equal to it.

hints.title: Value Range Bounding
hints.text: The possible values lie between the minimum element in the first column and the maximum element in the last column.

hints.title: Row Counting
hints.text: For a candidate mid value, count elements less than or equal to mid in each row using upper bound search.

hints.title: Matrix Value Range Search Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def matrixMedian(self, grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        low = min(row[0] for row in grid)
        high = max(row[-1] for row in grid)
        needed = (m * n + 1) // 2
        
        while low < high:
            mid = (low + high) // 2
            cnt = sum(bisect.bisect_right(row, mid) for row in grid)
            if cnt < needed:
                low = mid + 1
            else:
                high = mid
        return low
```

complexity.notes: Range search across value spectrum with bisect count per row.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Flattening and sorting the full grid takes O(mn log(mn)) time and O(mn) extra space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Binary searching over value range uses zero auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes monotonic count property of row-sorted matrices to avoid full sorting.
